verdict: KEEP — B grade confirmed. PIT clean, gentle DD 15/35 preserves more CAGR than tight DD 10/25 (+1.34pp), but both fail hurdle targets hard. Weak underlying alpha (IR negative, FF5 alpha ~0). DD overlay rescues MDD from 61.9% to 43.6% but not enough for production.

gate_0_pit.c1_full_sample_stats: PASS — no full-sample normalization. Z_Score_Aligned from Factor DB only.
gate_0_pit.c2_same_day_circular: PASS — DD brake uses t-1 lagged drawdown (line 62: dd_lagged <- c(0, dd[-n])). Explicitly C2 compliant.
gate_0_pit.c3_same_period_agg: PASS — no same-period aggregation. Sector demeaning is cross-sectional within each signal date.
gate_0_pit.c4_financial_lag: PASS — Factor DB handles financial statement lagging via Usable_Date.
gate_0_pit.c5_overlay_t_minus_1: PASS — DD brake uses dd_lagged (t-1). No other overlays.
gate_0_pit.c6_survivorship: PASS — RAWDATA includes delistings. Liquidity filter uses AvgTV20 with 1-day lag (shift(..., 1L, type='lag')).
gate_0_pit.c10_liquidity_filter: PASS — uses shift(frollmean(TradingValue, 20L), 1L, type='lag'). Prior-day 20d average.
gate_0_pit.c11_data_time_axis: PASS — Factor DB Z_Score_Aligned accessed on signal_date. No FRED or external time-series used.
gate_0_pit.c13_negate_factors: PASS — Z_Score_Aligned only, no manual sign flipping.
gate_0_pit.c15_factor_load: PASS — uses Arrow Dataset open_dataset() bulk load, not direct parquet.

gate_1_performance.assessment: FAIL — SR 0.404 far below 1.0 target. CAGR 7.1% far below 16% target. MDD 43.63% far above 25% limit. IR negative = underperforms benchmark. DD overlay reduced MDD from 61.9% (base) to 43.6%, saving ~18pp, but insufficient.

gate_3_role_honesty.assessment: HONEST — SR 0.404 too low for core_alpha. BM_Corr 0.746 is moderate-high, limiting diversification value. Negative IR confirms this is not a core alpha generator. Diversifier role is the most generous honest classification; borderline defense/diversifier.

gate_4_statistical.ic_assessment: FAIL — Full-period IC is essentially zero (-0.0007). The M25+V24 composite signal has no meaningful cross-sectional predictive power on average.
gate_4_statistical.oos_assessment: PASS — OOS SR (0.534) > IS SR (0.331), retention 1.61. Signal is NOT in-sample overfitted; if anything it improved OOS. This is the strategy's strongest statistical feature.
gate_4_statistical.alpha_trend_assessment: PASS — Recent 3Y SR (1.086) much higher than full-period (0.404). Factor is improving recently. But 20-year average is still weak.
gate_4_statistical.fmb_assessment: FAIL — Score factor FMB t-stat 0.130. Cross-sectional pricing power is statistically zero. Size factor is significant (t=-2.07), meaning returns are driven by size, not the M25+V24 signal.
gate_4_statistical.stress_test: PASS — 4/4 stress periods outperformed BM (GFC +4.05pp, COVID +4.77pp, Rate2022 +5.88pp, EuDebt +10.24pp). Defensive in crises.

gate_5_ff5.assessment: FAIL — FF3 and Carhart4 alphas are NEGATIVE (-1.3% to -1.4% annualized), though not statistically significant (|t| < 0.5). FF5 alpha is near zero (+0.47%, t=0.14). The strategy has NO independent alpha beyond known risk factors. All returns are explained by factor exposures (market, size, value, etc.).

dd1535_vs_dd1025.analysis: Gentle DD (15/35) wins on 6 of 7 metrics. Only MDD favors tight DD 10/25 by 1.74pp (41.89 vs 43.63). Gentle DD preserves +1.34pp CAGR and +0.031 SR. This REVERSES the STR_1509 meta-lesson where tight DD had better alpha survival. For M25 (weak base alpha), gentle DD is clearly superior because tight DD cuts too deep into an already thin return stream.

base_comparison.conclusion: DD overlay converted F to B. But 43.6% MDD still far from 25% target. The base alpha is simply too weak for DD alone to fix.

key_findings.strength_1: PIT fully clean — DD brake properly t-1 lagged, Factor DB Z_Score_Aligned, no violations
key_findings.strength_2: OOS retention 1.61 — signal is NOT overfitted, genuinely improves out-of-sample
key_findings.strength_3: Stress outperformance 4/4 — good crisis hedge behavior
key_findings.weakness_1: IC essentially zero (-0.0007) — no cross-sectional predictive power on average
key_findings.weakness_2: FF5 alpha is zero — all returns explained by known factors, especially size
key_findings.weakness_3: IR negative (-0.136) — underperforms benchmark over full period
key_findings.weakness_4: FMB Score t-stat 0.130 — factor has no pricing power; size drives returns

meta_lesson_dd_tightness.str_1509_finding: Tight DD had BETTER alpha survival (tight DD preserved SR better)
meta_lesson_dd_tightness.str_1527_finding: Gentle DD has BETTER alpha survival (+0.031 SR, +1.34pp CAGR)
meta_lesson_dd_tightness.reconciliation: The difference is base alpha strength. STR_1509 had meaningful alpha — tight DD clipped exposure wisely during drawdowns without destroying core returns. STR_1527's M25 has essentially zero alpha — tight DD's aggressive cash drag compounds the damage on an already weak signal. For weak-alpha strategies, gentle DD preserves the thin return margin; for strong-alpha strategies, tight DD protects capital without alpha loss.
meta_lesson_dd_tightness.generalized_rule: DD tightness should be calibrated to base alpha strength: strong alpha -> tight DD acceptable; weak alpha -> gentle DD or no DD at all.
